pairs.question: Cur igitur Christus ipse a coniugio abstinuit?
pairs.answer: Quasi uero non plurima sint in Christo, quae mirari potius quam imitari debeamus, sine patte natus, sine parentis dolore processit, clauso monumento prodiit.
pairs.derivation: Authorial diatribe question raised in the addressee's mouth. Dropped the framing tag 'inquies' (Cur igitur, inquies, Christus...). Answer ends at the first full stop after 'prodiit'; what follows (Quid in eo non supra naturam?...) is further rhetorical elaboration, not part of the direct reply. Kept the printed 'patte' verbatim, with no spelling normalization.

pairs.question: lam uero Mosaica lex sterile coniugium execratur, atque ob id a communibus aris quosdam submotos legimus. Quamobrem tandem?
pairs.answer: Nempe ideo quod tanquam inutiles, et sibi duntaxat uiuentes, populum nulla sobole augerent.
pairs.derivation: Author asks why the childless were removed from the common altars; setup sentence retained verbatim so 'tandem' has its referent ('quosdam submotos legimus'). Answer is the single sentence introduced by 'nempe ideo quod', normalized to initial capital; it ends at the full stop after 'augerent'. What follows ('Quod si lex damnat...') turns to a fresh inference, not the answer.

pairs.question: Fingunt ueteres illi ac sapientissimi poetae, quibus studium fuit philosophiae praecepta fabularum inuoluchris tegere, Gigantes anguipedes terrae filios, extructis in caelum montibus bellum superis intulisse. Quid haec sibi uult fabula?
pairs.answer: Nimirum immanes quosdam ac feros homines et obscuros, a coniugali concordia uehementer abhorruisse, eoque fulmine praecipitatos, hoc est, funditus interisse, cum id uitarent, quo solo constat humani generis incolumitas.
pairs.derivation: Author asks what the Giants fable means; the preceding sentence narrating the fable is kept verbatim so 'haec fabula' is intelligible. Answer is the single explanatory sentence beginning 'Nimirum', ending at the full stop after 'incolumitas'. What follows ('At iidem Orpheum...') begins a new fable, not the answer.

pairs.question: At iidem Orpheum poetam ac citharedum saxa durissima cantu mouisse commemorant. Quid signifcantes?
pairs.answer: Nempe uirum et sapientem et facundum, homines saxeos et ferarum ritu uiuentes, a uago concubitu prohibuisse, atque ad matrimonii sanctissimas leges adduxisse.
pairs.derivation: Author asks what the Orpheus fable signifies; the preceding sentence about Orpheus moving stones is kept so the question has a referent. Source spelling 'signifcantes' preserved verbatim. Answer is the single sentence beginning 'Nempe', ending at the full stop after 'adduxisse'. What follows ('Apparet igitur...') draws a conclusion, not the answer.

pairs.question: Hoc Thrax, hoc Sarmata, hoc Indus, hoc Graecus, hos Latinus, hoc uel extremus orbis Anglus, aut si qui sint his quoque semotiores, religiosum habuit. Quid ita?
pairs.answer: Quia necesse est omnibus esse commune, quod communis hominum parens inseuit, et adeo penitus inseuit, ut huius rei sensus non solum ad turtures et columbos, uerumetiam ad immanissimas feras pertingat, siquidem leones in uxorem mites sunt.
pairs.derivation: Author asks why all nations hold marriage sacred; preceding sentence kept so 'Quid ita?' has its antecedent. Answer is the single sentence introduced by 'quia', normalized to initial capital, ending at the full stop after 'sunt'. What follows ('Pro catulis dimicant tigrides.') is illustrative, beyond the direct answer.

pairs.question: Cur igitur praelata est uirginitas? cur honorata, si exitium adfert mortaliums?
pairs.answer: Laudata est, sed pro tempore, sed in paucis.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the objection (why is virginity preferred and honored, if it brings ruin?) and answers it. Source spelling 'mortaliums' preserved verbatim. Answer ends at the full stop after 'paucis'; what follows ('Voluit enim Deus...') is supporting explanation, not the core answer.
